title: Fractional coordinate precision
description:
The absolute precision of a set of fractional coordinates, in fractional units.

This describes how precisely the coordinates were *stated* by the source they came from,
which is generally coarser than the precision of the numbers as stored. A source that
writes a coordinate as `0.3333` claims it to about `0.0001` of a cell edge, however many
binary digits the value later occupies. It is the natural basis for choosing a matching
tolerance, a symmetry-detection parameter, or a grid spacing, in place of an arbitrary
constant.

**Requirements/Conventions**:

- The value is an **absolute** bound on the deviation from the intended value, not a
  relative precision and not a count of significant figures. A coordinate near `0.0001`
  and one near `0.9999` written to the same number of decimals have the same precision.
- The value is **dimensionless**, being a fraction of a cell edge. Multiplying by a cell
  length gives the corresponding precision as a distance; see
  [`length_precision`](https://schemas.anyterial.se/defs/v0.1/properties/core/length_precision).
- Where a set of coordinates is described by a single value, it SHOULD be the **coarsest**
  precision among them, since the set as a whole is only as precisely stated as its least
  precisely stated member.
- Where a source states both a number of digits and an explicit standard uncertainty, the
  value SHOULD be the larger of the two, that being the weaker and therefore the safer
  claim.
- The value MUST be strictly positive. A value of zero would assert exactness, which is a
  different claim; `null` MUST be used where the precision is unknown or where the source
  states an exact value rather than a measured one.
